methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Christopher Amidon that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three private companies in the ocean and maritime sector (Clippership, NetworkOcean, Albacore); no direct public comparables are available in this domain.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $10M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy. Applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $25M. This reflects the expected value increase associated with de-risking execution and market validation before Series A fundraising.

The triangulation analysis, constrained by a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median point of $25M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on stage-based progression rather than multiple independent approaches. Key uncertainties include the composition and trading multiples of the private peer set, which remain opaque; the applicability of the 2.5x multiplier to Standard Subsea's specific risk profile and market opportunity; and the company's progress toward Series A readiness. A more robust valuation would benefit from additional comparable transactions or revenue-based benchmarking within the maritime tech sector.
